messages:
Maya (Support): FYI customer Iris hit a weird reauth loop when using our embedded widget inside their SPA after SSO + MFA. They see the embedded iframe request a refresh token, then immediately get logged out. Repro steps and headers below.

Iris (Customer Success): Confirmed — if you open the app in an incognito top-level tab it works. Only happens when widget is run as an iframe inside our web app. This started after we rolled MFA enforcement for the org last week.

Maya (Support): Repro summary from customer: 1) User signs in via IdP (SAML/OIDC) on main site -> returns SSO session. 2) Embedded widget tries to call /session/refresh (POST) to exchange SSO assertion for device/session token. 3) Response sets cookie but widget then immediately gets 401 on next call and triggers front-end to show reauth modal. Loop.

Maya (Support): Customer sent the set-cookie header they saw on the refresh call:
```
Set-Cookie: rw_session=eyJ..; Path=/; Domain=.cust-example.com; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=3600
```
They also captured the console: iframe POST /v1/sessions/refresh -> 200, cookie present in response, but subsequent requests from iframe do NOT include cookie, so auth fails.

Raj (SRE): This screams SameSite blocking in a third-party iframe context. Browsers will block cookies with SameSite=Lax in cross-site iframe requests. The fact top-level tab works but iframe doesn't fits.

Ben (Eng): Agreed. For embedded widgets we should be setting SameSite=None; Secure. Otherwise cookie won't be sent. Also need Domain/Path consistent. Two potential fixes: (A) make the session cookie SameSite=None and Secure, or (B) switch to an explicit token response (postMessage handshake) instead of relying on browser cookies for iframe flows.

Iris (Customer Success): Is there a security tradeoff for SameSite=None? Our security team is nervous about third-party cookies.

Ben (Eng): SameSite=None means the cookie can be sent in third-party contexts, so you need Secure and ideally short TTL + HttpOnly. If you can't accept that, we can offer an explicit token-surface: the parent can receive the short-lived token on the top-level redirect and forward it into the iframe via postMessage. That avoids cross-site cookies.

Maya (Support): Customer also reported device trust flip: when MFA triggers rebind, device-jwt rotates and the widget seems to hold onto old device assertion. Their logs show status 428 from our /device/assert endpoint.

Maya (Support): Sample request/responses they pasted: 
```
POST /v1/sessions/refresh HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Content-Type: application/json
Origin: https://app.cust-example.com

Response 200 OK
Set-Cookie: rw_session=abc123; Path=/; Domain=.cust-example.com; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=3600

Next request from iframe: GET /v1/models  -> 401 (no cookie sent)
```

Raj (SRE): Another angle: if the embedded widget is on a different subdomain (widget.cust-example.com) vs main app (app.cust-example.com) check cookie Domain scoping; .cust-example.com should cover both, but if the iframe is served from a blob or another host it won't. Also ensure the embed isn't using data: or file: origins.

Iris (Customer Success): They're using widget-hosted-on-cdn.cust-example.com (CNAME to CDN). Domain=.cust-example.com should still match, but we can verify.

Ben (Eng): Can you ask them to test a quick repro change: set cookie from server to SameSite=None and see if requests from iframe include cookie? If they can't change that, we'll provide a code snippet for a postMessage fallback.

Maya (Support): Sent repro instructions. Also flagged that the SDK's default session refresh endpoint returns cookie-based sessions; there's an option `usePostMessageToken: true` in the embed config that will instead return a JSON token which the parent can pass into the iframe.

Iris (Customer Success): Customer tested toggling SameSite=None on their side and the loop stops — iframe sends cookie and sessions persist. They'd prefer not to flip global cookie policy though.

Ben (Eng): Ok for a safer short-term fix we can add a note in the embed README recommending the postMessage token flow for third-party contexts. Long term, consider making the widget auto-fallback to token exchange if it detects third-party cookie not present. Pseudocode:
```js
// embed init
if (document.hasStorageAccess) {
  // try cookie flow
} else {
  // request parent for token via postMessage
}
```

Maya (Support): Customer asked if this could also be causing device trust to fail (428). Any ideas?

Ben (Eng): Yes — if the widget doesn't get the refreshed device-jwt it will present an assertion that the server no longer recognizes. That triggers 428 (precondition required) for rebind. Ensuring the refresh token exchange reliably returns a token (via postMessage or SameSite=None cookie) should resolve both symptoms.

Raj (SRE): Quick mitigation we recommended to customer: 1) temporary set SameSite=None; Secure on cookie, 2) shorten cookie TTL to 5m during testing, 3) enable `usePostMessageToken` fallback in embed config. We'll keep monitoring.

Iris (Customer Success): Customer applied SameSite=None and confirmed flows stable. They'll roll out postMessage fallback before flipping org-wide cookie policy.

Maya (Support): I'll mark this as resolved for now but leaving notes for product/SDK team to make embed fallback more robust.

deploy-bot: deploy 2023-10-17T16:02:31Z: rolled out embed README update to staging docs. :white_check_mark:

Ben (Eng): Filed a small ticket to track auto-detect fallback: https://redwood.tracker/ISSUE-4271

Maya (Support): Thanks everyone. Closing the loop — customer happy for now, will re-open if they see anything else. :thumbsup:
